answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on paths from independently trusted sources rather than self-asserted identities. A sybil cluster may resemble a harbor beside a wharf on a broad river, but if few attestations cross its boundary, its conductance is low. Under bounded degree and walk length, conductance and min-cut bounds limit how much probability mass—and thus aggregate voting weight—can reach the cluster; transitivity does not multiply its influence without external links.
